title: First 2 Weeks
summary: Welcome to the team.
body:
## Your First 2 Weeks

### Day 1: Monday — BA Academy Day 1 · Office based (12:30 PM – 6:30 PM)

Welcome to the team. On Day 1 you'll get a full overview of the business, the direct sales industry, and the career opportunities ahead of you. You'll learn about earnings, incentives, and begin studying the sign-up process and presentation skills. Key focus: absorb everything, ask questions, and get excited about the opportunity.

### Day 2: Tuesday — BA Academy Day 2 · Office based (1:00 PM – 5:30 PM)

Deep dive into sales coaching in the office so you are ready for your 1st day on badge.

### Day 3: Wednesday — Practical Learning Day · Field based (10:00 AM – 5:30 PM)

Meet your coach and shadow them in the field. Watch how they approach doors, deliver the pitch, handle objections, and close sales. Take mental notes on body language, tone of voice, and energy levels. Key focus: observe the full sales cycle in action and start building your confidence.

### Day 4–5: Thursday & Friday — First Days on Badge (10:30 AM – 8:30 PM)

These are your first days delivering the pitch yourself in a live environment, with your mentor by your side to assist and support you. You will begin applying everything you have learned and making sales on your own badge. Mistakes are expected and are part of the learning process. Key focus: get comfortable with the opening and the flow of the conversation, build your confidence, and start developing your own rhythm on the doors.

### Day 6: Saturday — Badge Development & Consolidation (9:00 AM – 5:30 PM)

Day 6 is focused on consolidating and strengthening everything you have developed throughout your first week. This day gives you the opportunity to reinforce the skills and knowledge gained, gain further practical experience on badge, build greater confidence and independence, and address any areas that still require development or further clarification. The aim is to ensure you are well prepared to transition into your second week with greater capability and self-assurance.

### 2nd Week — Independent Growth

In your second week you'll begin working more independently. You'll develop territory management skills, learn to read different types of customers, and start setting personal daily targets. Your mentor will check in regularly but you'll be taking ownership of your day. Key focus: building self-reliance, hitting daily KPIs, and developing your own selling style. Every top performer started exactly where you are right now.

title: Our Expectations
summary: 100% Effort
body:
1. **100% Effort**  
   If you put 100% effort in you can achieve 100% results. Put 100% effort into anything you do.

2. **Be Proactive**  
   Don't wait for someone else, take control of your learning.

3. **Be Reliable**  
   Do what you say you are going to do.

4. **Willingness to Listen and Learn**  
   Always have your notepad ready to take notes and learn something new, if you don't understand, ask!

5. **Set Goals**  
   Have a why, set goals, work hard and hit those goals. If you have something you are working towards you are more likely to achieve.

6. **Be Positive**  
   Have a positive outlook, look for the solution rather than focusing on the problem.

7. **Great Customer Service**  
   We take pride in the work that we do and the service that we deliver.

8. **Pushing Boundaries**  
   Take a chance, give it a go. You will be surprised how much you can do when you try!
key_facts: 8 expectations: 100% Effort, Be Proactive, Be Reliable, Willingness to Listen and Learn, Set Goals, Be Positive, Great Customer Service, Pushing Boundaries

title: Learning Styles Questionnaire
summary: Pick the answer that feels most like you
body:
*Vertex Organisation Coaching Guide*

## Learning Styles Questionnaire

Pick the answer that feels **most like you**

**Question 1** — When spelling a word do you:

A. Try to see the word  
B. Sound out the word  
C. Write the word down to see if it looks right

**Question 2** — When talking in a group do you:

A. Use gestures & expressive movements to help make a point  
B. Try and create a story/picture with your message  
C. Like listening to other people's comments and input

**Question 3** — When trying to concentrate, which of the following MOST distracts you:

A. Sounds or noises  
B. Activity/movement around you  
C. Visual displays, or things that are out of place

**Question 4** — When meeting someone again do you:

A. Forget names but remember faces  
B. Forget faces but remember names or what you talked about  
C. Remember best what you did together

**Question 5** — I prefer:

A. Flicking through a newspaper or magazine  
B. Listening to news updates on the radio  
C. Watching news/current affairs updates on the television

**Question 6** — When receiving directions do you:

A. Prefer verbal directions  
B. Prefer a written diagram/map  
C. Step into your car and find your own way

**Question 7** — When installing a new appliance do you:

A. Ignore the instructions and figure it out as you go  
B. Get someone to read the manual and tell you what to do  
C. Follow the guidelines in the instruction manuals

**Question 8** — During a lecture or meeting do you:

A. Prefer to discuss it with others to secure your understanding  
B. Like to actively participate whenever possible  
C. Take detailed notes to help you remember information

**Question 9** — Of the following pick a career list that would interest you:

A. Writer, journalist, lawyer  
B. Artist, architect, engineer, mechanic, interior designer  
C. PE teacher, actor, fire-fighter, dancer, sportsman

**Question 10** — Which of the following best suits you:

A. I participate in sport and generally excel  
B. I enjoy listening to music and often sing or hum to myself  
C. I like to flick through magazines

### See your pattern emerge — Scoring Table

| Question | Visual | Auditory | Kinesthetic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1a | 1b | 1c |
| 2 | 2b | 2c | 2a |
| 3 | 3a | 3c | 3b |
| 4 | 4a | 4b | 4c |
| 5 | 5a | 5b | 5c |
| 6 | 6b | 6a | 6c |
| 7 | 7c | 7b | 7a |
| 8 | 8c | 8a | 8b |
| 9 | 9b | 9a | 9c |
| 10 | 10c | 10b | 10a |
| Totals | | | |

**Your learning style: Visual** — You are a visual learner — you think in pictures and learn best by seeing. Make the most of presenter cards, diagrams and written materials when on the doors.

**Your learning style: Auditory** — You are an auditory learner — you learn best through listening and talking. Role-play conversations, listen to the rehash audio, and talk through the steps out loud.

**Your learning style: Kinesthetic** — You are a kinesthetic learner — you learn best by doing. Get on the doors as quickly as possible and learn through real-world experience.

### Know your learning style

**Visual** `Average population: 35%`  `Marketing companies: 59%`

- Learn through seeing
- Think in pictures
- Often sit at the front to avoid obstructions
- May take detailed notes
- Need to see presenter's body language and facial expressions to fully understand content

**Auditory** `Average population: 25%`  `Marketing companies: 5%`

- Learn through what they hear
- Written information may have little meaning until heard
- Like to talk things through, be involved in discussion and listen to others

**Kinesthetic** `Average population: 40%`  `Marketing companies: 40%`

- Learn through moving, doing and touching
- They like to try things out
- Find it hard to sit still and can be easily distracted
- Like to move around and gesture when talking and may be poor listeners
key_facts: Visual — Average population: 35% · Marketing companies: 59%
Auditory — Average population: 25% · Marketing companies: 5%
Kinesthetic — Average population: 40% · Marketing companies: 40%

title: Body Language & S.E.E.
summary: S.E.E. Principle
body:
## S.E.E. Principle

### S — Smile

- Creates instant approachability and warmth
- Sets a positive tone that encourages engagement
- Builds initial trust — people are more open to hearing about the cause

### E — Eye Contact

- Shows confidence, honesty and respect
- Makes potential supporters feel valued
- Helps form genuine human connection — this is essential to build trust

### E — Enthusiasm

- Demonstrates authentic belief in the charity's mission
- Positive energy is contagious and inspires others to care
- Builds credibility — supporters trust genuine passion more than scripted sales

## Body Language

- **55%** Body movements, face, arms
- **38%** Tone of voice
- **7%** Words

> "It's never what you say, it's how you say it"

### Body Language

- One arm away from the door
- S.E.E. before you knock
- Weight on the back foot = relaxed
- Presenter card on the side
- Controlled hand gestures
- Use a pen to point at the presenter card
- Nod to show acknowledgment

### Tone of Voice

- Clear, concise and confident
- Enthusiastic
- Control the speed
- Use buzz words to keep engagement
key_facts: S.E.E. = Smile, Eye Contact, Enthusiasm
Body language 55% · Tone of voice 38% · Words 7%
"It's never what you say, it's how you say it"

title: The 5 Steps
summary: First impressions
body:
### 1 · Introduction — First impressions

- First impressions
- Ask engaging questions
- Who we are and why we're here

> "Hi there, how are you doing? I'm here on behalf of the National Deaf Children's Society. We're on a mission to get sign language into all the schools, do you know any sign language?"

### 2 · Present the Problem — Use need

- Paint the picture — invite compassion
- Pause and gain agreement
- Take your time, do not rush
- Match body language and tone to the message

> Every day in the UK, three babies are born deaf — and most deaf children are born to hearing parents. So you can imagine how tough that is, right?

### 3 · The Solution — What we do

- Reset the energy first — then sell the solution
- K.I.S.S — Keep it Short & Simple
- Speak with pride, passion and feeling
- Thank them after they agree

> What we do as a charity is amazing — we go into schools and homes to help parents and teachers communicate with deaf children, so they can do simple things like read a bedtime story.

### 4 · The Close — The ask

- They already know why you are here
- Point at the presenter card — show the amount
- Small amount, huge difference
- Be clear · Be confident · Be concise

> Knowing the difference you can make, can we get your help as well? My job is super simple — I send a form to your phone, you choose what you want to contribute, and you get a welcome call in the next 30–60 minutes.

### 5 · Rehash — Make it stick

- Reassure long-term commitment
- Cement the support so it lasts beyond today
- Make them feel like the hero
- What happens next: pop quiz + 3 thank you's

> Before I go, let me make sure you know exactly what happens next — so there are no surprises.

### Top Tips (use throughout)

- SEE Principle — Smile, Eye contact, Enthusiasm
- Statement, then question. Never two questions back to back
- Active listening — hunt for hotspots to relate to
- Mirror their energy — match the door, not your mood
- K.I.S.S — every extra sentence is a reason to say no
- Gain agreement before you ask. No agreement, no close
- Qualify, and walk away if it's not a fit. A wrong door costs you a right one

### The 3 Thank You's

1. **From you**  
   Thank you for taking the time to stop and support the children and families NDCS is here for.

2. **From NDCS**  
   On behalf of NDCS, thank you for choosing to make a difference every single month.

3. **From the children and families**  
   Every month when your donation goes out, your bank will send you a notification. That notification means a child somewhere is getting support — because of you.
key_facts: 1 Introduction · 2 Present the Problem · 3 The Solution · 4 The Close · 5 Rehash
Opening names the National Deaf Children's Society and sign language in schools
Problem line: three babies are born deaf every day in the UK; most deaf children are born to hearing parents
Close: form sent to the donor's phone; welcome call in the next 30–60 minutes
The 3 Thank You's: from you, from NDCS, from the children and families

body:

### The pattern

1. **Track the activity**

2. **Improve the conversion**

title: G.I.F.T.S
summary: Raising interest levels — when FRs are not getting to the close
body:
### Generosity

- The tremendous difference their support WILL make.
- Give them a BIG 'Thank You' when they agree to become an ongoing donor.
- Make sure the donor feels good about themselves for their selflessness.

### Indifference

- People love to buy but hate to be sold to; be genuine and natural, NOT pushy.
- Don't give the impression that you are desperate.
- Body language.
- Tone of voice.
- Step back when you get supporter concerns.
- Keep out of the donors' personal space.
- Learn to look relaxed.

### Feel Good Factor

- Paint mental pictures of the circumstances the charity is trying to overcome and what the unfortunate people, animals or environment might be going through.
- Evoke empathy in the donor about why their support is so very important. (“Thank you so much, if it wasn’t for people like yourself we wouldn’t exist as a charity.”)
- Use emotive language and tone of voice.

### Tone of Voice / Body Language

- Stress keywords and phrases.
- Use their name, if offered to you.
- Use assumption language.
- Match your body language with what you are saying, for example nod when asking 'yes' questions.

### Support

- People love to support when others are supporting too. They do not like to be the first or only one supporting.
- We've had great support from people in this area.
- Some of the people here are coming together to make a difference.
key_facts: G.I.F.T.S = Generosity, Indifference, Feel Good Factor, Tone of Voice / Body Language, Support

title: Addressing Supporter Concerns
summary: Listen first. Find the real concern. Respond with clarity.
body:
### Feel · Relate · Felt · Found · Re-close

**Feel**  
Let the donor know you care about the concern — empathise with them

↓

**Relate**  
Build a slight bond so it sounds natural — make them feel great here

↓

**Felt**  
Let the donor know this concern has previously been raised by other people

↓

**Found**  
Round the difference their small contribution will make to families

↓

**Re-Close**  
Having listened, empathised and reassured — close them

### Can Address

- Other charities
- One-off
- Bank details or don't want to give my details
- I'll do it online
- More information

### Cannot Address

- No door to door
- No direct debit
- Cannot afford
- Not interested

title: 8 Steps to Success
summary: A repeatable path from first day to long-term growth.
body:
1. **1 · Set a clear goal**  
   Know what you are working towards and why it matters.

2. **2 · Prepare your mindset**  
   Arrive ready to learn, listen and take responsibility.

3. **3 · Know your pitch**  
   Use the five steps with confidence and feeling.

4. **4 · Create genuine connection**  
   Smile, use eye contact and listen for what matters to them.

5. **5 · Present the problem and solution**  
   Make the need real, then show the charity solution.

6. **6 · Ask clearly**  
   Be direct about the monthly commitment and next steps.

7. **7 · Rehash every sign-up**  
   Make the commitment stick and protect supporter quality.

8. **8 · Review, learn and repeat**  
   Use the numbers and your coach to choose the next improvement.

## 5 Star Supporters

> The right people · The right impact · The right long-term supporter

> If the vast majority of the people you're signing up can tick off 4/5 or even 5/5 of these criteria, you know you're signing up the right people.

1. **Age**  
   42+

2. **High Street Bank**  
   70% Welcome Call answered

3. **Gift Aid**  
   Must be a UK taxpayer · Unless retired and maybe on a pension

4. **Opt Ins – Contact Details**  
   Email, phone and text opt in · Email opened · Barcode scanned

5. **Reason to Donate**  
   Do they have a connection to the cause?

> Focus on quality · Build loyalty · Create impact

### Common Fail Reasons

- Donor age: under 30 / over 75
- Changed mind
- Donor thought it was a one-off donation
- Pressure / spouse objected
- Cannot afford
- Inappropriate sign up: pressure by BA
- Incorrect contact details

> How to Avoid

- Qualify age correctly whilst on FIELD IQ: check over 30 and under 75 years old.
- Take time getting correct details and read back to donor to confirm. Fix on phone if necessary.
- Explain amount and that we are looking for long-term support clearly: show presenter card.
- Prepare the donor for the welcome call and reiterate importance: usually within 60 minutes from sign up.

title: What Is a No Show
summary: No show = first indicator of sign-up quality
body:
## What Is a No Show?

> Someone that's signed up but their first payment hasn't gone through. This has to be 85% and above for you to receive your 1st DD Quality Incentive.

### Why it happens

- Didn't have £12 in account
- Cancelled before first payment went out

> No show = first indicator of sign-up quality

## What does good look like?

*No show rate*

- **0–10%** Good
- **10–15%** Average
- **15–20%** Below
- **20%+** Bad

### 2 Things to Fix Quality

1. **Who You Sign Up**  
   Focus on signing up the right people — quality over quantity from the very first interaction.

2. **How You Sign Them Up**  
   The technique matters. Strong rehash builds commitment and filters out poor-quality sign-ups early.

> Start with the end goal in mind — long-term support is what we want!

### Communicate It

Make the long-term commitment crystal clear from the very first moment.

### Repeat It

Reinforce the message throughout the conversation — don't say it once and move on.

### Be Direct

Save time, effort and money by being upfront. No ambiguity, no wasted energy.

### Close with Clarity

The supporter should leave knowing exactly what they have signed up for.

### Red Flags — spot them early

- Can't afford it
- Asking for less than £12/month
- Asking for less than 12 months
- Making excuses
- Read body language cues
- Signs of vulnerability

> Quality supporters are easy! No red flags = smooth, committed sign-up.
key_facts: No show = signed up but first payment hasn't gone through
1st payment must be 85% and above to receive the 1st DD Quality Incentive
No show rate: 0–10% Good · 10–15% Average · 15–20% Below · 20%+ Bad
Red flags include asking for less than £12/month or less than 12 months

title: Welcome Call
summary: To emphasise the importance of answering the Welcome Call
body:
## Action Points for BAs to Tell Donors

*To emphasise the importance of answering the Welcome Call*

> Purpose of the Welcome Call — to ensure the donor understands the amount they are donating, that it is a long-term ongoing direct debit, and to gather feedback on their experience with us as Brand Ambassadors.

### 1st Attempt

Will happen within 60 minutes of them signing up — let them know this so they know when to expect the call. Get the donor to scan the QR code on the pitch card to save the contact, or manually save it in their contacts.

### Daily Attempts

The contact centre will continue to attempt at least twice a day, for up to 7 days from when they signed up, at different times of the day.

`Morning` `Afternoon` `Evening`

### Action points to tell donors

1. **Reassure them**  
   We give everyone a call in the next 60 mins to ensure they are happy and I have done my job correctly. — 020 4587 3738

2. **Save the number**  
   The call will come from this number so have that saved as NDCS. Please scan this QR code or manually save as a new contact. — 020 4587 3738

3. **Ask for commitment**  
   Please respond, it's very important for me and I'd love to count on you for this. Lots of eye contact before thanking them.

> Answering makes a big difference! Completed Welcome Call 70% and above → higher welcome calls = lower no-show rates = higher 3rd donation ratios = higher quality returns.

title: Closing with Clarity
summary: Diagnose it · Time it right · Re-close
body:
*Part 1 of 3 — Diagnose it*

### Why you're not closing — 4 reasons BAs don't close

1. **Confidence**  
   You don't back yourself. So you mumble, trail off, half-ask.

2. **Fear of Rejection**  
   You have personalised the no. So you avoid the ask to avoid the sting.

3. **Poor Example**  
   You've never seen it done right. Bad coaching gets copied.

4. **Not Enough Agreement**  
   You didn't build it. No yeses on the way up = no yes at the top.

> The Rule: An unclear close isn't a soft no. It's a sign-up you left at the door — and a deaf child who didn't get supported.

*Part 2 of 3 — The Impulse Curve*

### When & How to Close

Close above the giving line. Impulse rises, peaks, then dies — close at the peak. Slightly early beats too late.

1. **Be direct and clear**  
   No mumbling. No trailing off. They already know you're going to ask.

2. **Slow down and speak up**  
   Speed = doubt. The close is not the place to rush.

3. **Eye contact + gratitude**  
   Hold their eyes. Stay warm. Keep indifference — no big deal.

4. **Ask confidently — long term**  
   Chipping in £12 a month for as long as they can. Can we count on your support as well?

5. **Tell them what happens next**  
   Quick form to your phone, few details, direct debit starts in the next 3–4 weeks.

*Part 3 of 3 — The Redirect Scripts*

### Turn it. Re-close it.

A redirect is a buying sign — not a no.

> **One-Off Donation?**  
> Thank you, that's really generous! What we're actually asking is a small amount regularly so we can plan and budget — usually £12 a month for 12–18 months. Knowing that, could you squeeze us in as well?

> **Can I Do It Online?**  
> Absolutely — it's all a quick online form! I jot down basic details, send the form to your phone, get a reference number, and your direct debit starts in the next 3–4 weeks.

> **Small Amount?**  
> I know it doesn't sound like a lot — but when a lot of people do a small amount, it makes a huge difference. Can we count on your support as well?
key_facts: Part 1 Diagnose it (4 reasons: Confidence, Fear of Rejection, Poor Example, Not Enough Agreement)
Part 2 The Impulse Curve: close above the giving line, at the peak
Ask: £12 a month; direct debit starts in the next 3–4 weeks
Part 3 Redirect scripts: One-Off Donation?, Can I Do It Online?, Small Amount?

title: How to Use the COD
summary: The Proof Ladder, the 4 Pillars, the Weekly Rhythm and the Non-negotiables.
body:
## Cycle of Development

### The Proof Ladder

#### K · Know

Can explain it simply

#### D · Do

Can execute it effectively in the office

#### D · Deliver

Hits the standard under pressure in the field

#### T · Teach

Can transfer it to others

#### S · Systemise

Following proven systems to create independent examples of WGLL

### The 4 Pillars

#### Commercial Craft

The technical skills of the role. How you execute the sign up process, engage customers, handle questions, close confidently, and maintain quality under pressure. This is the foundation of performance.

#### Self Leadership

How you manage yourself. Your reliability, planning, resilience, emotional regulation, and ownership of your own results and development. No one can build this for you.

#### People Leadership

How you show up for and influence others. From following and enforcing standards as a BA, to coaching, developing, and holding a team accountable as a Leader.

#### Digital & Data

How you use numbers and systems. Accurate data submission, using KPIs to self-coach, tracking team performance, and making decisions driven by evidence, not feelings.

### Weekly Rhythm

- Choose the next stage and agree the outcomes and proof required
- Coach on the 4 pillars: Commercial Craft, Self Leadership, People Leadership, Digital & Data
- Review weekly: numbers, behaviour, evidence, decisions
- Drives results that are specific, owned and evidenced
- Progression only happens when evidence is shown and standards are consistently met
- Implement what good looks like (WGLL)

### Non-negotiables

- Standards are measured, owned and enforced with a consequence
- Data discipline: decisions are driven by numbers and evidence, not emotion
- Progression is a result of disciplined independence
key_facts: Proof Ladder: K Know · D Do · D Deliver · T Teach · S Systemise
4 Pillars: Commercial Craft, Self Leadership, People Leadership, Digital & Data
Progression is a result of disciplined independence

## Stage 1: Foundation

### Evidence Required

- Three consecutive days with great time ownership and effort
- Can demonstrate the 5 step sign up process and handle common objections in office role play and in a live environment
- Field IQ completed with no missing fields

### What Good Looks Like

#### Commercial Craft

- Runs the full sign up process in the correct order without missing any steps. Sounds confident and conversational, not rehearsed.
- Creates immediate connection. The customer/donor can hear the smile in your voice. Your eye contact shows you are present and trustworthy. Your enthusiasm shows you genuinely believe in what you’re talking about.
- Closes the sign up clearly and confidently, turning the customer/donor’s interest into a clear commitment.
- Handles common questions and campaign specific objections by listening, using systems, understanding the real concern and checking it has been resolved before re-closing.
- Can articulate the impulses and use them naturally throughout the conversation. Able to identify where and how each one should be used.
- Stands in the right place, uses open, confident and engaging posture, hand movements and gestures to build trust and show enthusiasm. Respects personal space.

- Respects start times and schedules, prepared and ready to work. Can be relied upon to manage themselves without needing reminders or follow up.
- Does not let one bad interaction affect the next ones. Responds to rejection quickly and resets for the next opportunity. Stays productive instead of becoming emotional or discouraged. Can separate outcomes from their attitude and effort.
- Demonstrates emotional resilience and remains consistent even when faced with challenges. Can separate personal circumstances from professional performance.

#### People Leadership

- Demonstrates discipline and effort without needing supervision or recognition. Knows WGLL for quality standards and KPIs.
- Keeps updates clear. Raises issues appropriately and professionally.
- Flags challenges, asks questions and uses support correctly so problems can be solved quickly.

#### Digital & Data

- Makes Field IQ part of their daily routine.
- Understands and applies LOA to drive consistent results.
- Can articulate and understands the importance of achieving quality KPIs. Shows actions of how to maintain high quality sign ups.

### What Good Looks Like

#### Commercial Craft

- Can teach the psychology behind customer/donor decision making and coach BAs to apply it naturally, ethically and effectively. Can teach elevated, next level sign up skills.
- Can coach the cause/USP of a specific campaign. Uses quality data to identify coaching priorities proactively rather than reacting once they appear. Helps BAs understand why quality matters. Follows up to ensure behavioural changes.
- Continues to build 1st generation Leaders who can lead, coach and make decisions effectively without relying on them.
- Doesn’t need to personally carry the team’s numbers. Delegates responsibility instead of becoming the bottleneck. Moves from being the producer of results to the builder of people who produce results.

#### Self Leadership

- Separates the person from the performance problem. Doesn’t become defensive when challenged. Can reset quickly after a difficult coaching interaction. Maintains consistency: the team doesn’t have to judge what “mood” their Leader is in.
- Doesn’t avoid or allow conflict to drag on. Doesn’t confuse fairness with keeping everyone happy. Moves the team forward once the issue has been resolved.
- Can identify when culture and atmosphere are contributing to retention or performance problems and takes action. Creates and protects an environment where positives and high standards are something that people want to be part of. Has both a fun and professional team culture that remains strong without depending solely on the Owner.
- Knows the key numbers that determine office profitability. Personally budgets and plans ahead. Invests in people for development and growth.

#### People Leadership

- Sets expectations with Leaders clearly, with specifics. Standards enforcements are communicated quickly and consistently.
- Can observe another Leader coaching and improve their coaching ability, showing visible improvements through data. Coaching through the full leadership loop.
- Develops people who can think and solve problems without constantly verifying, to build independence. Coaching through the full leadership loop.
- Can coach people to focus on controllables and appropriate actions. Builds the person’s ability to navigate the next cycle independently.

#### Digital & Data

- Able to find root causes. Can teach Leaders how to understand and use their own KPIs.
- Can distinguish a one-off dip from an emerging pattern. Uses tools like AI and automation to catch what a manual review would miss. Can anticipate problems early through patterns.
- Keeps team reporting accurate and consistent.
- Tracks movement through each stage, not just overall headcount. Can identify when and where people are dropping out. Holds Leaders accountable for the progression and retention of people.

### Standards & Consequences

- Continue maintaining and building on COD 3 standards
- Not just verbal leadership: every standard must have a metric and a consequence
- If underperformance repeats, actions must be documented and time bound
- Repeated misses equals paused progression
- Maintain profitability and quality standards

### Tools & Systems

- Team Scorecard
- Recruitment IQ

title: Quality Payments — how they work
summary: Quality payments are paid 4 months after the sign-up month.
body:
## Quality Payments Calculator

Quality payments are paid 4 months after the sign-up month.

### How quality payments work

1. **The gate**  
   Your quality rate must be at or above 70% to qualify for any payment that month.
2. **3rd donation**  
   Sign-ups who reach their 3rd direct debit are your qualifying supporters: sign-ups × quality rate.
3. **Payment**  
   You get £15 per qualifying supporter, paid 4 months after the sign-up month. For example, September sign-ups are paid in January.

Projections assume the same quality rate every month. Actual payments depend on 3rd direct debits confirmed by the charity, and the 70% gate must be met in each individual month.
key_facts: The gate: your quality rate must be 70% or above to qualify for any payment that month
Qualifying supporters = sign-ups who reach their 3rd direct debit
£15 per qualifying supporter
Paid 4 months after the sign-up month — September sign-ups are paid in January
